ajay.patel: Hey team — quick question. I-485 pending, filed I-131 (advance parole) and EAD still processing. Planning short travel next month and might return on AP. Can I start as an employee before the EAD card arrives? What do I need for I-9, benefits enrollment, and payroll?
Maya - People Ops: Short version — you can’t complete I-9 Section 2 until you present acceptable original documents in person in the US. Section 1 can be done remotely, but Section 2 must be done within 3 business days of your start date if you’re physically in the US. If you’re outside the US on the start date, we can’t onboard as a new employee until you return and we examine docs.
Maya - People Ops: If you re-enter on Advance Parole and have an AP stamp + passport (or AP stamp on passport) and an I-94 showing admission, that satisfies List A for I-9 for employment authorization. EAD card is not strictly required if you have AP admission evidence. :white_check_mark:
ajay.patel: OK — so if I return on AP and show passport + I-94 we can complete I-9 and retroactively start? I have a USCIS receipt for EAD but card won’t be here for a few weeks.
Maya - People Ops: Yes, once we see the passport with AP admission/I-94 we can complete Section 2 and set your official employee start date to the date you presented docs (or another agreed date). Payroll can be backdated to that date if needed, within payroll cutoff rules.
payroll-bot: FYI payroll details: we need the completed I-9 + direct deposit + W-4 on file before first pay run. If we backdate, we need clear written approval from the hiring manager. Tax residency will be determined by your work location on the payroll start date. If you’re abroad at the time, there are potential withholding and benefits implications — we’ll need to coordinate.
Liam Chen: We can do a contractor-bridge for up to 4 weeks if Ajay needs to start earlier for project ramp. I can approve contractor hours; payroll, please advise on vendor setup timeline.
payroll-bot: Contractor bridge option: vendor/contractor pay requires vendor onboarding (1–2 business days if urgent), PO approval, and will be paid via contractor payroll, not employee benefits. If you choose contractor bridging, benefits enrollment will happen when employee status begins.
Maya - People Ops: Action items: 1) Ajay — if you plan travel, please scan and upload your USCIS receipt and any flight/entry itinerary to the onboarding portal so we can track. 2) When you return, bring original passport showing AP admission/I-94 to People Ops for Section 2. 3) If you need contractor bridge, confirm and Liam will submit approval.
people-ops-bot: Links: Onboarding upload -> https://okta.redwoodinference/onboard (upload scans), I-9 guidance -> https://docs.redwoodinference/hr/i9-remote.md, Contractor policy -> https://docs.redwoodinference/hr/contractor-bridge.md
ajay.patel: Thanks — one more: is there any way to expedite biometrics/EAD timeline? USCIS receipt number  MSC123456789.
Maya - People Ops: USCIS expedite is case-by-case; we can provide a letter of employment if USCIS asks but they rarely grant expedite for EAD production. If you want us to send a support letter, DM me the receipt and reason for expedite. Also consider using AP entry to avoid waiting on card, as discussed.
ajay.patel: I'll upload the receipt tonight and DM you, Maya. If contractor bridge is needed I'll ask Liam to kick it off. Appreciate the clarity. :slightly_smiling_face:
Liam Chen: Sounds good. If you need anything from our side for the USCIS letter, ping me. Happy to confirm the project timeline.
Maya - People Ops: Great — we’ll follow up with a checklist after you upload. Reminder: always bring originals for I-9; scans are just for pre-check.
ajay.patel: Got it, thanks everyone! :pray:
